title: Stuffing a la Alinea
description: We made this for our Women’s Resource Dinner one year – “A Little Like Alinea” – and it was delicious and easy enough to make again, especially for Thanksgiving.
ingredients: 75 g leek, white part, finely diced
600 g good bread, w/o crust, finely diced
a leg or two of goose/duck meat (confit)
a leg or two of goose/duck skin
directions: In small, dry skillet, toast celery seed over medium heat for 5 minutes, or until fragrant. Reserve.

In a medium saucepan, combine onions, fennel, celery, leek, and garlic over low heat. Add 150 g of goose/duck fat and sweat vegetables for 5 minutes. Transfer to sheet tray and let cool to room temperature.

In medium bowl, combine bread, eggs, stock, toasted celery seed, orange zest, nutmeg, salt, pepper, goose/duck leg meat, and remaining 150 g of goose/duck fat. Stir to combine. Let rest for 30 minutes to allow bread to absorb excess moisture. Stir in cooled vegetables.

Preheat over the 375 degrees. Spray medium (9” x 13”) shallow pan with nonstick cooking spray. Line bottom of pan with goose skin and a single, even layer. Spoon stuffing mixture over skin in even layer. Cover pan with foil. Bake for 45 minutes to 1 hour, or until top springs back to touch. Remove from oven and let cool.
Place second shallow pan on top of stuffing, and top pan with weights to press firmly. Refrigerate overnight.
For serving, cut stuffing into bars, turn skin side up, and broil briefly until warmed and nicely colored.
